Series::random_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series& Series::random_() const
Series& Series::random_(std::int64_t to) const
Series& Series::random_(std::int64_t from, std::int64_t to) const

What It Does¶

Overwrites every element of the receiver with a uniformly chosen integer:

  • random_() — from [0, upper) where upper depends on the receiver dtype (see the table below).

  • random_(to) — from [0, to).

  • random_(from, to) — from [from, to).

The interval is half-open: from is reachable, to is not. The draw is always integer-valued; if the receiver is floating-point, the integers are stored as floating values like 5.0 — random_ never becomes continuous sampling. This makes it the right primitive for IDs, offsets, bucket indices, and categorical codes. For a continuous fill, use uniform_.

The no-argument upper per dtype:

receiver dtype

random_() range

Bool

[0, 2) — i.e. {0, 1}

Int8

[0, 128)

UInt8

[0, 256)

Int16 / UInt16

[0, 32768) / [0, 65536)

Int32 / UInt32

[0, 2^31) / [0, 2^32)

Float16 / BFloat16 / Float32

[0, 2^24)

Int64 / UInt64 / Float64

[0, 2^53)

Reproducibility¶

Deterministic given the process-wide RNG seed. Call pluss::rng_seed(seed) before sampling to fix the values; two runs from the same seed produce equal tensors. Each call advances a stream counter.

Parameters¶

from (std::int64_t): the (inclusive) lower bound. Defaults to 0.

to (std::int64_t): the (exclusive) upper bound. Must be > from, and the whole [from, to) range must be representable in the receiver dtype.

Returns¶

Series& A reference to the receiver, now holding the integer draws. The write is in-place and preserves storage identity — every alias sees the values.

Raises¶

  • if to <= from

  • if [from, to) does not fit the receiver dtype

  • if the receiver’s dtype is complex

Gradient¶

Not differentiable.

Examples¶

Example 1. random_(to) — integers in [0, to). Seeded, so fixed.

pluss::rng_seed(42);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({12}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);
x.random_(10);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[12], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[8, 1, 2, 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 9, 2, 0, 8]

Every value is in 0..9; 10 never appears.

Example 2. random_(from, to) — a signed range, with to excluded.

pluss::rng_seed(7);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({12}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);
x.random_(-2, 3);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[12], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[-1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, -2, -1, 2, 2]

The draws come from {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2} — 3 is out.

Example 3. On a floating receiver the draws are still integers, stored as X.0.

auto x = pluss::series::empty({8}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.random_(5, 6);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[8], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[5.0000, 5.0000, 5.0000, 5.0000, 5.0000, 5.0000, 5.0000, 5.0000]

Only integer 5 is in [5, 6). This is not the same as uniform_(5.0, 6.0), which would fill with continuous values.

Example 4. A large sample from [0, 100) is uniform over the 100 integers.

pluss::rng_seed(3);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({200000}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);
x.random_(0, 100);
auto v = x.host<int>();
long lo = 1'000'000'000, hi = -1'000'000'000; double sum = 0;
for (int e : v) { lo = std::min<long>(lo, e); hi = std::max<long>(hi, e); sum += e; }
std::cout << "min=" << lo << "  max=" << hi << "  mean~" << sum / v.size() << "  (expect ~49.5)\n";

Output¶

min=0  max=99  mean~49.466

Example 5. The range must fit the dtype; complex receivers and a non-increasing range are rejected.

try {
  auto i8 = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Int8);
  i8.random_(0, 300);              // 300 > INT8_MAX
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto c = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Complex64);
  c.random_(0, 5);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto i = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);
  i.random_(5, 5);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

random_: requested range is outside the receiver dtype
random_: complex receivers are not supported
random_: expected hi > lo

Example 6. Reproducible under a fixed seed.

pluss::rng_seed(9);
auto a = pluss::series::empty({6}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64); a.random_(0, 1000);
pluss::rng_seed(9);
auto b = pluss::series::empty({6}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64); b.random_(0, 1000);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "a == b: " << a.equal(b) << "\n";

Output¶

a == b: true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • random_ is integer-valued, always. On a floating receiver the values are whole numbers stored as floats — it is not uniform_.

  • to is excluded. random_(n) draws from 0..n-1.

  • The whole [from, to) range must be representable in the receiver dtype — a wide range into a small integer type, or into a low-precision float that cannot hold every distinct integer, is rejected.

  • Complex receivers are rejected (no ordered integer interval for complex).

  • Reproducible only after pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call advances the stream.

  • Not differentiable.

Summary¶

random_() / random_(to) / random_(from, to) fills the receiver in place with uniform integers from a half-open range:

  • always integer-valued, even on a floating receiver (stored as X.0)

  • default range depends on the receiver dtype (see the table)

  • to excluded; range must fit the dtype; complex rejected

  • reproducible under pluss::rng_seed(seed); not differentiable; aliases see the write

See Also¶

  • Series::uniform_: the continuous counterpart — [from, to) over the reals, not the integers.

  • Series::multinomial: non-uniform category selection.

  • pluss::series::randint: create an integer tensor instead of filling one.

  • Series::bernoulli_: the {0, 1} special case with a tunable probability.
